notes: CANDIDATE - not closed and single-origin. Blackstone-owned AirTrunk is finalising the underwriting group for an A$4.3bn (~US$3.0bn, FX-converted hence amount_estimated=1) five-year syndicated loan to build SYD3, a 400+MW hyperscale campus in Western Sydney. Named underwriters: Credit Agricole, DBS, Deutsche Bank, HSBC, ING, MUFG, Morgan Stanley, UOB, with the group still expanding. ESCALATION: traced back through TFTC, TradingView, Yahoo, FreeMalaysiaToday, The Star and Mingtiandi - every one of them cites the same Bloomberg report, so this counts as ONE source, not six (circular-reporting guard). The earlier Jun 18 Bloomberg piece had AirTrunk merely 'seeking' $3bn, so this is a real progression, but no borrower, sponsor or lender release exists yet.

CANDIDATE - EARLY-STAGE TALKS, nothing committed. Blue Owl's STACK Infrastructure is seeking an A$8.5bn (~US$5.9bn, FX-converted hence amount_estimated=1) syndicated loan for its third Melbourne data centre; Bloomberg explicitly notes bank talks are early and terms may change. Would be one of the largest data-centre financings ever done in Australia. Blue Owl acquired STACK through its takeover of IPI Partners. Single origin (Bloomberg; The Edge Malaysia and Mingtiandi both re-report it). Tension worth flagging: STACK is simultaneously weighing a sale of Australian, Japanese and Malaysian assets reportedly valued at >$30bn, and Blue Owl's flagship private-credit funds were gate-capped at 5% on Jul 2 against $4.7bn of redemption requests - raising and de-risking at the same time.

CANDIDATE - STATED PLAN, NOT COMMITTED CAPITAL (amount_estimated=1). President/COO Jonathan Gray told Nikkei that Blackstone intends to invest ~$30bn in Japanese AI data centres over the next three to five years, exploring projects exceeding 1GW combined against >500MW already built. No vehicle close, no signed deal, no counterparty disclosed. Single source (one Nikkei interview). Partial corroboration of intent: Blackstone hired Ami Momaya as Head of Infrastructure for India on Jul 16, consistent with an APAC infrastructure buildout, but that is adjacent, not confirming.

CANDIDATE - the in-window event is the DEBT, not the acquisition. Four banks (BNP Paribas, Goldman Sachs, HSBC, Mizuho) wrapped a $1.75bn loan package backing SoftBank's $5.375bn purchase of ABB's robotics division. Priced at 98.5 OID with a 4.25pp margin on both the dollar and euro tranches; the dollar piece was upsized by $200m to $800m on US leveraged-loan demand. round_total_usd = the $5.375bn purchase price. The ACQUISITION ITSELF WAS SIGNED 2025-10-08 AND HAS NOT CLOSED - still pending EU, China and US clearance, targeted mid-to-late 2026 - so no control has changed hands. Single origin (Bloomberg; TradingView/Yahoo/briefs.co all re-report). Escalation: no SoftBank Group IR release covers the financing; the Jul 29 68th/69th unsecured straight bond issuance is separate corporate funding.

CANDIDATE - EXPLORATORY, no final decision on size or structure. SoftBank is weighing an acquisition of Zurich-based Gravis Robotics AG (2022 ETH Zurich spinout, autonomous construction equipment) at a valuation reportedly >$500m (amount_estimated=1). Would be held in a NEW entity SoftBank is setting up called Roze, an AI-and-robotics holdco it intends to list in the US; SoftBank has separately been consolidating robotics assets under a holdco called Robo HD. Deal could be staged across secondary share purchases plus primary capital injections. Gravis last raised $23m in November. Single origin (Bloomberg, carried by SWI swissinfo). Corroborating exhaust for the wider thesis: SoftBank completed its Boston Dynamics exit to Hyundai in mid-July, i.e. it is rotating out of legacy robotics into AI-native robotics.
